[[lint-rules]]
= Lint rules

Each rule shows a case from the linter's tests: the original code, what `Linter.fix` makes of it, and what `Linter.lint` reports, with `[fix]` after the findings that come with a fix.

[cols="3,1,8"]
|===
|Rule |Severity |Description

|<<lint-syntax-error,`syntax-error`>>
|error
|The code does not parse, or breaks a rule Nix checks while parsing, such as defining an attribute twice. No other rule runs then.

|<<lint-unused-let-binding,`unused-let-binding`>>
|warning
|A `let` binding that the body never reaches. A binding used only by itself, or by other unused bindings, counts as unused too. The fix removes it.

|<<lint-unused-lambda-arg,`unused-lambda-arg`>>
|warning
|A function argument that the body never uses. The fix renames it to `_`, unless the body uses an outer `_`.

|<<lint-unused-formal,`unused-formal`>>
|warning
|An attribute of a function's pattern that the body never uses. It is not reported when the `@` binding is used, as that may pass it on. The fix removes it only when the pattern has `+...+`, so that callers passing it still work.

|<<lint-unused-at-pattern,`unused-at-pattern`>>
|warning
|An `@` binding that the body never uses. The fix removes it.

|<<lint-bool-comparison,`bool-comparison`>>
|warning
|A comparison with `true` or `false`. There is no fix: `v == true` is also a type test, where `v` alone fails on other types.

|<<lint-bool-simplification,`bool-simplification`>>
|warning
|`!(a == b)`, which is `a != b`, and `!(a != b)`, which is `a == b`.

|<<lint-empty-let-in,`empty-let-in`>>
|warning
|A `let` with no bindings.

|<<lint-collapsible-let-in,`collapsible-let-in`>>
|warning
|A `let` right in the body of another. The fix merges them unless the outer bindings use or bind a name of the inner ones.

|<<lint-legacy-let-syntax,`legacy-let-syntax`>>
|warning
|The deprecated `+let { ...; body = ...; }+`. The fix turns it into `+rec { ...; body = ...; }.body+`.

|<<lint-empty-inherit,`empty-inherit`>>
|warning
|An `inherit` with no names.

|<<lint-empty-pattern,`empty-pattern`>>
|warning
|A function taking `{ }`. There is no fix: `_:` would also accept arguments that are not an empty attribute set.

|<<lint-redundant-pattern-bind,`redundant-pattern-bind`>>
|warning
|`+{ ... }@x: body+`, which can be written `x: body`.

|<<lint-manual-inherit,`manual-inherit`>>
|warning
|`a = a;` in an attribute set that is not recursive, which is `inherit a;`.

|<<lint-manual-inherit-from,`manual-inherit-from`>>
|warning
|`a = e.a;`, which is `inherit (e) a;`.

|<<lint-eta-reduction,`eta-reduction`>>
|hint
|`x: f x`, which is `f` when `f` is a name or an attribute path that does not use `x`.

|<<lint-useless-parens,`useless-parens`>>
|warning
|Parentheses around a simple expression, or around a whole binding value, `let` body, interpolation or file.

|<<lint-unquoted-uri,`unquoted-uri`>>
|warning
|A URI literal, which is deprecated. The fix quotes it.

|<<lint-deprecated-is-null,`deprecated-is-null`>>
|warning
|`isNull e`, which is `e == null`.

|<<lint-deprecated-to-path,`deprecated-to-path`>>
|warning
|`builtins.toPath`, which is deprecated. There is no fix.

|<<lint-empty-list-concat,`empty-list-concat`>>
|warning
|A concatenation with `[ ]`.

|<<lint-useless-has-attr,`useless-has-attr`>>
|warning
|`if x ? a then x.a else d`, which is `x.a or d`.

|<<lint-faster-builtin,`faster-builtin`>>
|hint
|`lib.groupBy` and `lib.zipAttrsWith`, which the builtins of the same names implement natively.

|<<lint-repeated-keys,`repeated-keys`>>
|hint
|Three or more bindings that start with the same attribute, such as `a.b`, `a.c` and `a.d`, which could form one nested attribute set. There is no fix.

|<<lint-undefined-variable,`undefined-variable`>>
|error
|A variable that no binding defines, outside any `with`. Nix rejects the file before evaluating it.

|<<lint-unknown-builtin,`unknown-builtin`>>
|error
|`builtins.x` where `x` is not a builtin, unless the file tests `builtins ? x` or gives an `or` fallback.

|<<lint-prefixed-builtin,`prefixed-builtin`>>
|warning
|`__x` for the builtin `builtins.x`.

|<<lint-shadowed-builtin,`shadowed-builtin`>>
|warning
|A binding that hides a global such as `map`, `true` or `builtins`. Attributes of a `rec` set and names inherited from an expression are not reported.

|<<lint-extra-rec,`extra-rec`>>
|warning
|A `rec` attribute set whose attributes never refer to each other.

|<<lint-extra-with,`extra-with`>>
|warning
|A `with` that no variable can come from.

|<<lint-missing-phase-hooks,`missing-phase-hooks`>>
|warning
|A phase such as `installPhase` set to a string that does not run its hooks: nixpkgs expects `runHook preInstall` first and `runHook postInstall` last, so that `preInstall` and `postInstall` still work. The fix adds the missing calls to strings of several lines.

|<<lint-missing-final-attrs,`missing-final-attrs`>>
|warning
|A derivation built from a `rec` set whose attributes refer to each other, such as `+stdenv.mkDerivation rec { ... }+`. With `+finalAttrs: { ... }+`, an override of `version` through `overrideAttrs` also reaches the attributes that use it. The fix rewrites the references to `finalAttrs.version` and the like. For builders other than `stdenv.mkDerivation`, `finalAttrs` holds the attributes the builder made, so the fix is only offered when the references are to `pname`, `version` and `src`.

|<<lint-missing-structured-attrs,`missing-structured-attrs`>>
|hint
|A derivation that does not set `__structuredAttrs`, which nixpkgs expects to be `true` for new packages. The builders that default it to `true`, such as those for Python, are not reported. The fix adds `__structuredAttrs = true;` after `pname` and `version`; it changes the build, since phases then see lists as Bash arrays, so check that the package still builds.

|<<lint-missing-strict-deps,`missing-strict-deps`>>
|hint
|A derivation that does not set `strictDeps`, which nixpkgs expects to be `true` for new packages. The builders that set it already, such as those for Python, Go and Rust, are not reported. The fix adds `strictDeps = true;` after `pname` and `version`, or under `__structuredAttrs`; it changes the build, since tools must then be in `nativeBuildInputs` and libraries in `buildInputs`, so check that the package still builds.

|===

== Syntax errors

[[lint-syntax-error]]
=== `syntax-error`

Severity: error. The code does not parse, or breaks a rule Nix checks while parsing, such as defining an attribute twice. No other rule runs then.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{
  a = 1;
  a = 2;
}
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
syntax-error.nix:3:3: error[syntax-error]: attribute 'a' already defined
----

== Dead code

Bindings that nothing uses, as https://github.com/astro/deadnix[deadnix] finds them. Names starting with `_` are never reported.

[[lint-unused-let-binding]]
=== `unused-let-binding`

Severity: warning. A `let` binding that the body never reaches. A binding used only by itself, or by other unused bindings, counts as unused too. The fix removes it.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{ f }:
let
  used = 1;
  unused = 2;
  self = x: self x;
  a = b;
  b = a;
  _ignored = 3;
  inherit (f) kept dropped;
  inherit (f) gone;
  nested.x = 1;
  nested.y = 2;
  # Only `dead` is reported: the uses of `ver` and `pkg` are inside it too.
  dead = ver: pkg: pkg.${ver};
in
[
  used
  kept
]
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{ f }:
let
  used = 1;
  _ignored = 3;
  inherit (f) kept;
  # Only `dead` is reported: the uses of `ver` and `pkg` are inside it too.
in
[
  used
  kept
]
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
unused-let-binding.nix:4:3: warning[unused-let-binding]: unused let binding 'unused' [fix]
unused-let-binding.nix:5:3: warning[unused-let-binding]: unused let binding 'self' [fix]
unused-let-binding.nix:6:3: warning[unused-let-binding]: unused let binding 'a' [fix]
unused-let-binding.nix:7:3: warning[unused-let-binding]: unused let binding 'b' [fix]
unused-let-binding.nix:9:20: warning[unused-let-binding]: unused let binding 'dropped' [fix]
unused-let-binding.nix:10:15: warning[unused-let-binding]: unused let binding 'gone' [fix]
unused-let-binding.nix:11:3: warning[unused-let-binding]: unused let binding 'nested' [fix]
unused-let-binding.nix:14:3: warning[unused-let-binding]: unused let binding 'dead' [fix]
----

[[lint-unused-lambda-arg]]
=== `unused-lambda-arg`

Severity: warning. A function argument that the body never uses. The fix renames it to `_`, unless the body uses an outer `_`.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
let
  ignored = x: 1;
  underscore = _x: 1;
  used = x: x;
  # Renaming `y` to `_` would capture the outer `_`.
  capture = _: y: _;
in
[
  ignored
  underscore
  used
  capture
]
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
let
  ignored = _: 1;
  underscore = _x: 1;
  used = x: x;
  # Renaming `y` to `_` would capture the outer `_`.
  capture = _: y: _;
in
[
  ignored
  underscore
  used
  capture
]
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
unused-lambda-arg.nix:2:13: warning[unused-lambda-arg]: unused lambda argument 'x' [fix]
unused-lambda-arg.nix:6:16: warning[unused-lambda-arg]: unused lambda argument 'y'
----

[[lint-unused-formal]]
=== `unused-formal`

Severity: warning. An attribute of a function's pattern that the body never uses. It is not reported when the `@` binding is used, as that may pass it on. The fix removes it only when the pattern has `+...+`, so that callers passing it still work.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
[
  ({ a, b, ... }: a)
  # Without `...`, removing `b` would change which arguments are accepted.
  ({ a, b }: a)
  # `args` may pass `b` on.
  ({ a, b, ... }@args: args)
  ({ a, b ? a, ... }: b)
  (
    {
      a,
      b,
      c,
      ...
    }:
    c
  )
]
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
[
  ({ a, ... }: a)
  # Without `...`, removing `b` would change which arguments are accepted.
  ({ a, b }: a)
  # `args` may pass `b` on.
  ({ a, b, ... }@args: args)
  ({ a, b ? a, ... }: b)
  (
    {
      c,
      ...
    }:
    c
  )
]
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
unused-formal.nix:2:9: warning[unused-formal]: unused formal argument 'b' [fix]
unused-formal.nix:4:9: warning[unused-formal]: unused formal argument 'b'
unused-formal.nix:10:7: warning[unused-formal]: unused formal argument 'a' [fix]
unused-formal.nix:11:7: warning[unused-formal]: unused formal argument 'b' [fix]
----

[[lint-unused-at-pattern]]
=== `unused-at-pattern`

Severity: warning. An `@` binding that the body never uses. The fix removes it.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
[
  (args@{ a, ... }: a)
  ({ a, ... } @ args: a)
  (args@{ a, ... }: args)
]
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
[
  ({ a, ... }: a)
  ({ a, ... }: a)
  (args@{ a, ... }: args)
]
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
unused-at-pattern.nix:2:4: warning[unused-at-pattern]: unused pattern binding 'args' [fix]
unused-at-pattern.nix:3:17: warning[unused-at-pattern]: unused pattern binding 'args' [fix]
----

== Simpler forms

Code with a simpler or more idiomatic form, as https://github.com/oppiliappan/statix[statix] finds it.

[[lint-bool-comparison]]
=== `bool-comparison`

Severity: warning. A comparison with `true` or `false`. There is no fix: `v == true` is also a type test, where `v` alone fails on other types.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{ x, y }:
[
  (x == true)
  (false != y)
  (x == y)
]
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
bool-comparison.nix:3:4: warning[bool-comparison]: comparison with 'true'; if the other side is always a boolean, use it directly
bool-comparison.nix:4:4: warning[bool-comparison]: comparison with 'false'; if the other side is always a boolean, use it directly
----

[[lint-bool-simplification]]
=== `bool-simplification`

Severity: warning. `!(a == b)`, which is `a != b`, and `!(a != b)`, which is `a == b`.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{ a, b }:
[
  (!(a == b))
  (!(a != b) || a)
  (!(a && b))
]
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{ a, b }:
[
  (a != b)
  (a == b || a)
  (!(a && b))
]
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
bool-simplification.nix:3:4: warning[bool-simplification]: negated comparison; use '!=' [fix]
bool-simplification.nix:4:4: warning[bool-simplification]: negated comparison; use '==' [fix]
----

=== `empty-let-in`

Severity: warning. A `let` with no bindings.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original

let
in

  a = let in 1;
}

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed

  a = 1;
}

empty-let-in.nix:1:1: warning[empty-let-in]: 'let' with no bindings [fix]
empty-let-in.nix:4:7: warning[empty-let-in]: 'let' with no bindings [fix]

[[lint-collapsible-let-in]]
=== `collapsible-let-in`

Severity: warning. A `let` right in the body of another. The fix merges them unless the outer bindings use or bind a name of the inner ones.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{
  merged =
    let
      a = 1;
    in
    let
      b = a;
    in
    b;
  # Merged, the inner `b` would replace the argument in `a = b;`.
  capture =
    b:
    let
      a = b;
    in
    let
      b = 2;
    in
    a + b;
}
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{
  merged =
    let
      a = 1;
      b = a;
    in
    b;
  # Merged, the inner `b` would replace the argument in `a = b;`.
  capture =
    b:
    let
      a = b;
    in
    let
      b = 2;
    in
    a + b;
}
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
collapsible-let-in.nix:6:5: warning[collapsible-let-in]: this 'let' can be merged into the outer one [fix]
collapsible-let-in.nix:16:5: warning[collapsible-let-in]: this 'let' can be merged into the outer one
----

[[lint-legacy-let-syntax]]
=== `legacy-let-syntax`

Severity: warning. The deprecated `+let { ...; body = ...; }+`. The fix turns it into `+rec { ...; body = ...; }.body+`.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
let {
  x = 1;
  body = x;
}
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
rec {
  x = 1;
  body = x;
}.body
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
legacy-let-syntax.nix:1:1: warning[legacy-let-syntax]: legacy 'let { }' syntax; use 'let ... in' [fix]
----

[[lint-redundant-pattern-bind]]

  ({ a, ... }@args: args)
]
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
[
  (args: args)
  (args: args)

[[lint-manual-inherit]]
=== `manual-inherit`

Severity: warning. `a = a;` in an attribute set that is not recursive, which is `inherit a;`.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{ a, b }:
{
  plain = {
    a = a;
  };
  # In a `rec`, `b = b;` refers to itself.
  recursive = rec {
    b = b;
  };
}
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{ a, b }:
{
  plain = {
    inherit a;
  };
  # In a `rec`, `b = b;` refers to itself.
  recursive = rec {
    b = b;
  };
}
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
manual-inherit.nix:1:6: warning[unused-formal]: unused formal argument 'b'
manual-inherit.nix:4:5: warning[manual-inherit]: 'a = a;' can be written 'inherit a;' [fix]
----

[[lint-manual-inherit-from]]
=== `manual-inherit-from`

Severity: warning. `a = e.a;`, which is `inherit (e) a;`.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{ pkgs, lib }:
{
  hello = pkgs.hello;
  name = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.name;
  options = (lib.evalModules { modules = [ ]; }).options;
  lib = lib.lib;
  other = pkgs.notOther;
  fallback = pkgs.fallback or null;
}
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{ pkgs, lib }:
{
  inherit (pkgs) hello;
  inherit (pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform) name;
  inherit (lib.evalModules { modules = [ ]; }) options;
  inherit (lib) lib;
  other = pkgs.notOther;
  fallback = pkgs.fallback or null;
}
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----
manual-inherit-from.nix:3:3: warning[manual-inherit-from]: can be written 'inherit (...) hello;' [fix]
manual-inherit-from.nix:4:3: warning[manual-inherit-from]: can be written 'inherit (...) name;' [fix]
manual-inherit-from.nix:5:3: warning[manual-inherit-from]: can be written 'inherit (...) options;' [fix]

----

----

[[lint-useless-parens]]
=== `useless-parens`

Severity: warning. Parentheses around a simple expression, or around a whole binding value, `let` body, interpolation or file.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----

  atom = f (a);
  select = (a.b).c;
  fallback = f (a.b or null);
  call = (f a) a;
  interpolation = "${(f a)}";
  string = f ("x");
  nested = f ((a));
  tight = f(a);
  tighter = f((a));
  path = f(./x);
  operator = (a + a) * 2;
}
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{ f, a }:
{
  value = f a;
  atom = f a;
  select = a.b.c;
  fallback = f (a.b or null);
  call = (f a) a;
  interpolation = "${f a}";
  string = f "x";
  nested = f a;
  tight = f a;
  tighter = f a;
  path = f ./x;
  operator = (a + a) * 2;
}
----

== Packaging

Conventions of nixpkgs for derivations.

[[lint-missing-phase-hooks]]
=== `missing-phase-hooks`

Severity: warning. A phase such as `installPhase` set to a string that does not run its hooks: nixpkgs expects `runHook preInstall` first and `runHook postInstall` last, so that `preInstall` and `postInstall` still work. The fix adds the missing calls to strings of several lines.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{ stdenv }:
stdenv.mkDerivation {
  pname = "example";
  version = "1.0";

  installPhase = ''
    mkdir -p $out/bin
    cp example $out/bin/
  '';

  # Only the missing call is added.
  buildPhase = ''
    runHook preBuild
    make
  '';

  checkPhase = ''
    runHook preCheck
    make check
    runHook postCheck
  '';

  # Not fixed: the calls need lines of their own.
  configurePhase = "./configure --prefix=$out";
  fixupPhase = ''true'';
}
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{ stdenv }:
stdenv.mkDerivation {
  pname = "example";
  version = "1.0";

  __structuredAttrs = true;
  strictDeps = true;

  installPhase = ''
    runHook preInstall

    mkdir -p $out/bin
    cp example $out/bin/

    runHook postInstall
  '';

  # Only the missing call is added.
  buildPhase = ''
    runHook preBuild
    make

    runHook postBuild
  '';

  checkPhase = ''
    runHook preCheck
    make check
    runHook postCheck
  '';

  # Not fixed: the calls need lines of their own.
  configurePhase = "./configure --prefix=$out";
  fixupPhase = ''true'';
}
----

[source,text,role="secondary"]
.Diagnostics
----

missing-phase-hooks.nix:2:1: hint[missing-strict-deps]: set 'strictDeps = true;' [fix]
missing-phase-hooks.nix:6:3: warning[missing-phase-hooks]: 'installPhase' does not run 'runHook preInstall' and 'runHook postInstall' [fix]
missing-phase-hooks.nix:12:3: warning[missing-phase-hooks]: 'buildPhase' does not run 'runHook postBuild' [fix]
missing-phase-hooks.nix:24:3: warning[missing-phase-hooks]: 'configurePhase' does not run 'runHook preConfigure' and 'runHook postConfigure'
missing-phase-hooks.nix:25:3: warning[missing-phase-hooks]: 'fixupPhase' does not run 'runHook preFixup' and 'runHook postFixup'
----

[[lint-missing-final-attrs]]
=== `missing-final-attrs`

Severity: warning. A derivation built from a `rec` set whose attributes refer to each other, such as `+stdenv.mkDerivation rec { ... }+`. With `+finalAttrs: { ... }+`, an override of `version` through `overrideAttrs` also reaches the attributes that use it. The fix rewrites the references to `finalAttrs.version` and the like. For builders other than `stdenv.mkDerivation`, `finalAttrs` holds the attributes the builder made, so the fix is only offered when the references are to `pname`, `version` and `src`.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{
  stdenv,
  fetchurl,
  buildPythonPackage,
  fetchPypi,
  lib,
}:
{
  hello = stdenv.mkDerivation rec {
    pname = "hello";
    version = "2.12";
    src = fetchurl {
      url = "mirror://gnu/hello/${pname}-${version}.tar.gz";
      hash = "sha256-AAAA";
    };
    passthru = {
      inherit lib version;
    };
    meta.changelog = "https://example.org/${version}";
  };

  # Other builders give `finalAttrs` what they made of `meta`, so only `pname`, `version` and `src` are rewritten.
  python = buildPythonPackage rec {
    pname = "example";
    version = "1.0";
    src = fetchPypi { inherit pname version; };
    passthru.homepage = meta.homepage;
    meta.homepage = "https://example.org";
  };

  fixable = buildPythonPackage rec {
    pname = "other";
    version = "2.0";
    src = fetchPypi { inherit pname version; };
  };

  # Not fixed: the inner `finalAttrs` would capture `pname` and `version`.
  nested = stdenv.mkDerivation rec {
    pname = "nested";
    version = "1.0";
    modules = stdenv.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {
      pname = "${pname}-modules";
      inherit version;
    });
  };

  # Left to `extra-rec`: no attribute refers to another.
  plain = stdenv.mkDerivation rec {
    pname = "plain";
  };
}
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{
  stdenv,
  fetchurl,
  buildPythonPackage,
  fetchPypi,
  lib,
}:
{
  hello = stdenv.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {
    pname = "hello";
    version = "2.12";

    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;
    src = fetchurl {
      url = "mirror://gnu/hello/${finalAttrs.pname}-${finalAttrs.version}.tar.gz";
      hash = "sha256-AAAA";
    };
    passthru = {
      inherit lib; inherit (finalAttrs) version;
    };
    meta.changelog = "https://example.org/${finalAttrs.version}";
  });

  # Other builders give `finalAttrs` what they made of `meta`, so only `pname`, `version` and `src` are rewritten.
  python = buildPythonPackage rec {
    pname = "example";
    version = "1.0";
    src = fetchPypi { inherit pname version; };
    passthru.homepage = meta.homepage;
    meta.homepage = "https://example.org";
  };

  fixable = buildPythonPackage (finalAttrs: {
    pname = "other";
    version = "2.0";
    src = fetchPypi { inherit (finalAttrs) pname version; };
  });

  # Not fixed: the inner `finalAttrs` would capture `pname` and `version`.
  nested = stdenv.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {
    pname = "nested";
    version = "1.0";

    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;
    modules = stdenv.mkDerivation (_: {
      pname = "${finalAttrs.pname}-modules";
      inherit (finalAttrs) version;

      __structuredAttrs = true;
      strictDeps = true;
    });
  });

  # Left to `extra-rec`: no attribute refers to another.
  plain = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "plain";

    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;
  };
}
----

.Diagnostics

missing-final-attrs.nix:9:11: hint[missing-strict-deps]: set 'strictDeps = true;' [fix]

missing-final-attrs.nix:23:31: warning[missing-final-attrs]: use 'finalAttrs: { ... }' instead of 'rec { ... }'

[[lint-missing-structured-attrs]]
=== `missing-structured-attrs`

Severity: hint. A derivation that does not set `__structuredAttrs`, which nixpkgs expects to be `true` for new packages. The builders that default it to `true`, such as those for Python, are not reported. The fix adds `__structuredAttrs = true;` after `pname` and `version`; it changes the build, since phases then see lists as Bash arrays, so check that the package still builds.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{
  stdenv,
  buildGoModule,
  buildPythonPackage,
  buildHomeAssistantComponent,
  pname,
  version,
}:
{
  plain = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "plain";
    version = "1.0";

    strictDeps = true;
  };

  final = stdenv.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {
    inherit pname version;
    meta.description = "${finalAttrs.pname} example";
  });

  go = buildGoModule {
    # The comment stays with `src`.
    src = ./.;
    vendorHash = null;
  };

  set = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "set";
    __structuredAttrs = true;
  };

  # Deliberately off.
  off = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "off";
    __structuredAttrs = false;
  };

  # Defaults to `true`.
  python = buildPythonPackage {
    inherit pname version;
  };

  # So does Home Assistant's builder.
  component = buildHomeAssistantComponent {
    inherit pname version;
  };
}
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{
  stdenv,
  buildGoModule,
  buildPythonPackage,
  buildHomeAssistantComponent,
  pname,
  version,
}:
{
  plain = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "plain";
    version = "1.0";

    strictDeps = true;
    __structuredAttrs = true;
  };

  final = stdenv.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {
    inherit pname version;

    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;
    meta.description = "${finalAttrs.pname} example";
  });

  go = buildGoModule {
    __structuredAttrs = true;

    # The comment stays with `src`.
    src = ./.;
    vendorHash = null;
  };

  set = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "set";
    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;
  };

  # Deliberately off.
  off = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "off";
    __structuredAttrs = false;
    strictDeps = true;
  };

  # Defaults to `true`.
  python = buildPythonPackage {
    inherit pname version;
  };

  # So does Home Assistant's builder.
  component = buildHomeAssistantComponent {
    inherit pname version;
  };
}
----

.Diagnostics

missing-structured-attrs.nix:17:11: hint[missing-structured-attrs]: set '__structuredAttrs = true;' [fix]

[[lint-missing-strict-deps]]
=== `missing-strict-deps`

Severity: hint. A derivation that does not set `strictDeps`, which nixpkgs expects to be `true` for new packages. The builders that set it already, such as those for Python, Go and Rust, are not reported. The fix adds `strictDeps = true;` after `pname` and `version`, or under `__structuredAttrs`; it changes the build, since tools must then be in `nativeBuildInputs` and libraries in `buildInputs`, so check that the package still builds.

[source,nix,role="primary"]
.Original
----
{
  stdenv,
  buildGoModule,
  buildDotnetModule,
  pname,
  version,
}:
{
  # The two fixes put both flags together.
  both = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "both";
    version = "1.0";

    src = ./.;
  };

  structured = stdenv.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {
    inherit pname version;

    __structuredAttrs = true;

    meta.description = "${finalAttrs.pname} example";
  });

  set = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "set";
    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;
  };

  # Deliberately off.
  off = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "off";
    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = false;
  };

  # Go's builder sets it already.
  go = buildGoModule {
    __structuredAttrs = true;
    src = ./.;
  };

  dotnet = buildDotnetModule {
    inherit pname version;
    __structuredAttrs = true;
  };
}
----

[source,nix,role="secondary"]
.Fixed
----
{
  stdenv,
  buildGoModule,
  buildDotnetModule,
  pname,
  version,
}:
{
  # The two fixes put both flags together.
  both = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "both";
    version = "1.0";

    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;

    src = ./.;
  };

  structured = stdenv.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {
    inherit pname version;

    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;

    meta.description = "${finalAttrs.pname} example";
  });

  set = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "set";
    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;
  };

  # Deliberately off.
  off = stdenv.mkDerivation {
    pname = "off";
    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = false;
  };

  # Go's builder sets it already.
  go = buildGoModule {
    __structuredAttrs = true;
    src = ./.;
  };

  dotnet = buildDotnetModule {
    inherit pname version;
    __structuredAttrs = true;
    strictDeps = true;
  };
}
